memory: I wake up around 7:00 AM every day. The first thing I do is check my schedule for the day and make a to-do list. I prioritize my tasks based on their importance and deadlines. I usually start with responding to any urgent emails or messages from professors or classmates. After that, I head to the gym for a quick workout to get my blood pumping. It's a great way to clear my mind and prepare for the day ahead. Post-workout, I grab a quick breakfast and head to my first class, which is usually a lecture or a lab session. I make sure to take detailed notes and engage with the material to make the most of my time.I usually wake up around 6:30 in the morning. It’s become a habit ever since I started wanting to get a head start on projects—though some days, especially if I was up late coding or gaming, I might sneak in an extra 15 minutes or so. The first thing I do is check my calendar on my phone, just to get my head around what’s coming up that day. Then I do some basic stretching right there beside my bed, so I’m not half-asleep when I jump in the shower. I’ve found that if I skip the stretches, I’m sluggish for at least an hour or so, and let’s be honest—who has time for that?After my morning routine, I head to the gym for a quick workout. It’s a great way to get my blood pumping and clear my mind. I try to make it a habit to go at least three times a week, but if I’m really busy, I might have to skip a session or two. It’s not ideal, but it’s better than nothing. Once I’m done with my workout, I grab a quick breakfast and head to my first class, which is usually a lecture or a lab session. I make sure to take detailed notes and engage with the material to make the most of my time.In the afternoons, I often have more classes or lab sessions. I make sure to stay focused and engaged, taking notes and participating in discussions. I find that the afternoon classes are just as important as the morning ones, as they cover different topics and build upon the material from earlier in the day. By the time I finish my last class, I feel satisfied knowing that I’ve made progress towards my degree.After my last class, I usually have some free time before dinner. I use this time to relax and unwind. I might watch a movie, read a book, or catch up on some TV shows. It’s essential to take breaks and recharge to avoid burnout. I also make sure to stay connected with friends and family through social media or phone calls. It’s great to have such a supportive network of loved ones who care about my well-being.Dinner is another highlight of my day! I often meet up with friends or family at a restaurant or cook a meal at home. It’s a great opportunity to enjoy good food and spend quality time with the people I care about. I make sure to eat a balanced meal and stay hydrated throughout the day. By taking care of my physical health, I can maintain the energy levels needed to tackle the demands of being a CS major.In the evenings, I usually spend some time working on any remaining assignments or projects. I try to make progress on the most challenging tasks first, so I can feel a sense of accomplishment as the day comes to a close. I also use this time to review my notes and prepare for the next day’s classes. By staying organized and on top of my work, I can ensure that I’m making the most of my time and meeting my academic goals.As the day winds down, I take a moment to reflect on what I’ve accomplished. I make a mental note of any tasks that need to be completed the next day and update my to-do list accordingly. By staying organized and focused, I can maintain a sense of control and confidence in my ability to manage my time effectively. It’s not always easy, but it’s worth it to achieve my goals and make the most of my college experience.After a quick shower, I’ll head to the kitchen in my off-campus apartment. I live with two roommates—one’s also a CS major, the other’s a mechanical engineering major. Usually, we’re all hustling to get out the door. If I’m feeling ambitious, I’ll whip up some scrambled eggs and spinach, maybe have a piece of whole wheat toast, and brew coffee using one of those single-cup machines we all share. If I’m rushed, I’ll just grab a granola bar and some fruit to eat while I head to campus. I try to be economical with time while making sure I eat something relatively nutritious. I’m pretty active, so I can’t slack on breakfast too often.Once I’m fueled up, I head to campus, usually around 8:00 AM. I make sure to arrive at my first class with a few minutes to spare, so I can get settled and ready to go. I find that getting to class early helps me stay focused and avoid distractions. By being prepared and organized, I can make the most of my time and set myself up for success.In the afternoons, I often have more classes or lab sessions.
